description: A Roman inscription found in the mid 19th CE at the Roman fort of Bewcastle (identified as Fanum Cocidii). The inscription had been used in the field wall between the north-west corner of the church yard and Demesne far, where it was recovered by Maughan. It references the construction of a temple for Jupiter Optimus Maximus of Doliche (Jupiter Dolichenus). The original location of the temple is unknown, presumably its use was co-terminus with that of the fort, placing it in an early 2nd CE - late 4th CE date range.
bibliography: “RIB 992. Dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus of Doliche | Roman Inscriptions of Britain.” Inscription. Accessed April 7, 2026. https://romaninscriptionsofbritain.org/inscriptions/992.
